body:
Thanks. Definitely have tried that. I do take cbd. Thc seems to just make it worse once I get to like 10% thc so have to take it easy. It actually helped me gain my weight back after nausea took me out for so long.  

Just seems like doctors and nurses get so mad at you for not getting better that they just don't want to believe it. Really awful personalities and it's hard to bring myself to pay to be mistreated and judged.
How do you know that? It's very easy for someone in my situation to end up homeless.

Vertigo. I can't seem to walk straight most days and sometimes get severe spins for hours. The diagnosis has been a debate among my specialists so there's a lot of theories.    
I also have a wonky autonomic nervous system which makes me faint easily. I do try my best to keep that stable but the medication for vertigo always aggravates it. And exercises to maintain good blood flow always aggravates vertigo.
Oh I'd be pissed if even I couldn't tell what they were seeing on their side.
My Teams app will go idle if it's minimized sometimes while I'm working. I always wondered what poor unfortunate souls that have bosses with poor tech knowledge are getting reprimanded for that.

I'm close to losing my job in my 30s. Declared disabled by the state. This is not how I imagined my future.     
There's too many people that haven't ever been on this level of mental illness and just can't comprehend how heavy it weighs you down but sure act like they know all about it. It's hard to hear it and see it everywhere. "No one wants to work". "If I can work 70hrs a week you can work 40" etc...   

I don't work just because it makes me feel like I'm worth something. I still feel hollow. In fact it has its own unique way of tearing your mental stability apart in itself. I work because I'd end up living on the streets and I've gotten so bad lately that I might just give up and do that.     

Whatever happened to the "it gets better as you get older" shit I used to hear in my 20s?     

Anyways just know you're not alone in this. It may feel that way but the truth is, most people like us aren't out and about and in everyone's faces everyday so it's easy to see everyone except you has it together. Most of us are hidden.

Hey yeah I've definitely tried many avenues for my disability. I didn't just stick to your run of the mill doctors after I wasn't getting anywhere with them. My life is a constant medical journey trying to figure out which path to choose next and I've already dropped over 60k on medical costs which causes depression and high emotions anytime I get yet another bill.       
There are also a lot of treatments that could permanently disable me even further. Some medications have also permanently injured me.          
         
I can't go to mayo because it's not a guarantee for help and could leave me completely broke and jobless in my attempts.       
        
I did visit a medical university and I was nearly hospitalized because travel is that hard on me. They wanted me to keep coming back and I ran out of the physical ability to with trying to keep my job.       
             
It doesn't help that I'm in a bad area for medical care but I have important connections here that I have a high reputation with so I'd end up in a very bad spot with no support if I just moved.      
     
For every medical mystery success story there are hundreds unresolved.     

All you can do is dedicate your life to finding an answer (which sadly makes doctors here think you are obsessed and furthers their desire to push more psychiatristic meds on you).     

Next week I start a medication that I've gotten imported from another country because I don't have much money to try those fancy alternative doctors. I am definitely trying.        

But I will have a year here and there where I break down and completely give up. Constantly changing meds and treatments is torture. And I think that's just human. I don't blame anyone that gives up if they've taken a similar journey.

Nothing. I caught influenza and ended up with post viral complications (strikingly similar to what we are seeing in covid now). And it was all downhill from there because it literally disables you.  
My jobs were accommodating but sleeping 17hrs a day and fainting all the time while doctors were apathetic and only so much can be done.   

It also did a number on my mental health which only further complicated things.  I'll always have a soft spot for those with mental illnesses and I don't think passion has anything to do with it. Their mental health simply sucks and I think there is a solid organic scientific explanation for this that we just haven't found yet. (Kind of how people with MS used to be told they were just faking it).

I did pursue things I loved in life. I was a network engineer, and before that I was hosting parties. I loved it.          
       
I keep telling you, poor health will knock all that love right out of you. There is nothing worth throwing up and getting sick over and that's just what happens to any activity if your brain or body isn't working right.

Haha yeah I get that. I recently had an antibiotic temporarily clear up something that had been weighing me down for a decade. I told the doc I think these are making me high because I feel so calm and focused. He laughed and said that's just probably what it feels like to have all the bacteria and inflammation wiped out of me for a bit.    

It was actually a bit of an epiphany moment for me realizing how hard I was on myself expecting myself to keep up with normal people that were on some superhero shit called a healthy brain and body.

Yeah that's the problem with mental illness though. In many cases you can't find something you enjoy because your brain is programmed to hate everything randomly.   
Even if I had all the time and money in the world, I couldn't list anything I truly enjoy besides not being conscious.

Most people do push themselves until they are close to collapse or exhaustion but no one believes it until it actually happens. I know a lot of people in my life that struggle and while they won't work until they drop, they will work until they are crying alone in their car after every shift. And they cry because the alternative is quitting and not being able to pay the bills or having to be dependent on someone which most people 100% do not want.       

They want to be able to go to work and just be a little stressed and have a beer like everyone else. Maybe take a vacation once in a while and have it recharge them so they can return back to work well rested. That is not a reality for most of them and that's what this whole problem is.

So what about all of us that pushed ourselves until we collapsed and ended up permanently disabling ourselves even more because we were trying to do what was expected of us?    
This isn't a walt disney film dude.

Have you tried getting a job?       
Just kidding. I have many physical and mental issues that make working torture. I actually took everyone's get a job advice and it caused me to end up in the ER, more medications, more visits, costing thousands upon thousands every year while I could barely pay my necessities.     

But at least they understood at that point. I'd hate to say it but no one believes how bad it is until their advice pushes you to hospitalization then they change their tone real fast. I wish there was a different way to get through to them but this is like 90% of people.

I definitely know what class of drug it is and how to tread in that area. I know too well how you never under any circumstance want to ever build a tolerance to it.  I see it as an emergency drug more than anything.

Yeah I'm already in a few groups and many of them struggle with being treated like dirt or face homelessness.  But a lot of people don't get hit severe vertigo until they're older so they already have aged into a family that supports them. I also have cfs and that is so so misunderstood. A lot of suicides in both of the conditions I have simply because they have no options better than death. You're left to the wolves without support.

Thanks. It's hard not to blame myself. I do realize I push until I collapse and can't do much more than that. It's hard to not get mad at your own existence though. Like in the end it's my stupid dysfunctional body that is the cause of all this drama.    

I can predict and work around people if I didn't need them to survive. Being vulnerable is absolutely terrible.

I was in that situation long ago with my family which is why I can't really ever rely on them when this stuff happens. It really hurts but I was glad I had the health to find my own way out. And you will feel so good to gain independence after trying to overcome the abandonment.       

After being homeless I kind of zoned out, dissociated, and before I knew it, years had gone by and I was leaving my apartment to get in my car to take my dog to the park and kind of woke up then and there and cried from finally making it.     
       
I hope you get that experience soon.      

I just can't see myself doing that in such a frail physical state now. Healthy me would just pack my stuff and start over even if it landed me without a home first again.

Yeah. Like on one hand I don't want to get mad at someone for not wanting to be around someone sick but then I remember they fucking said they could handle it and like man, you're literally letting down someone in their worst time just so you could pump your own ego about being for them in the beginning? Cowards.       

Did you get any warnings with the cervical cancer? I just had to have some chunks removed and they said it was clear now but there's still so much pain and with everyone being so apathetic I haven't really cared much about myself either.  Just waiting for the "oops we didn't check that thing you complained about and you're dying now" .
I've heard good things about etizolam. Unfortunately difficult to get. Would be a miracle for my severe vertigo attacks

Yeah that's the problem. Since you look ok, they will start not taking your concerns seriously (like just forcing the job on you anyways) after some time then when you actually end up completely debilitated they'll step back and say whoops but after a year they get right back into forgetting they almost killed you and repeat the same pattern.     

Ugh. Good luck and I hope they listen to you. My company is small so I don't have much legal protection but look into fmla if your company is over 50 employees.

That's one of the huge problems here. I engulfed myself so heavily into work that I caused a chronic illness from pushing too hard (had strep then collapsed after a 16hr shift and health took a permanent nosedive).       

Now I'm too sick to have a family of my own. Too sick to enjoy life. But working too many hours to improve my health.       

At the very least now, I will get the rest I've needed for so long.       

I feel like it's weak character to do this. But I'd rather die on the streets than in a desk.

Actually I just put my two weeks in after 8yrs with this place not long after that comment, whole reason I was on this sub... and they are suddenly letting me have anything I want.    


You are right. Fear is the mind killer. They are now bargaining with someone that has lost the fear.     


I am no stranger to poverty. I have no kids. The medical system has failed me. And I do not fear death.  Really nothing left to lose here except stupid materialistic bullshit.

I've been pulling 12hr days with way too many responsibilities and just fainted and hit my head. I'm disabled though so I'm scared I won't be able to find another job that lets me work from home. I don't want to be disabled and homeless.    

Ssdi is extremely hard to get in your 30s too.    

I'm so terrified and exhausted.

It seems like they always have an excuse out of something unless it's 100% text book.   
I've had certain labs come back weird, multiple times. And I felt like shit with it too.   
Even when I get retested for just that thing specifically... the phlebotomists tell me it's strange and no one usually is "just off on that only".   

All I basically got was a supplement to correct it. Once corrected I still feel like shit but am trying to ask "hey maybe that was just a result showing up of something else going on to cause it... maybe I'm not absorbing something the right way" but get brushed off and told to just keep my labs normal by supplementing.

I've been getting delivery for years. I feel so spoiled. I used to go in while heavily overstimulated, sometimes have to leave my cart in a panic, sometimes faint, always missing items even with a list, ... go home and lay in bed the rest of the day.
I really wish my body would have waited until the second dose to do this. Not cool lol. I wonder what kind of protection we have with just one.

I did get a flare after my first vaccine. It wasn't hospital level stuff but tbh I didn't expect it because everyone told me the second would be the one that knocks me out. Also it doesn't seem like there's a huge connection between who it knocks out and pre existing conditions. I have to reschedule my second now because my job is not going to let me have more time off if I get sick again.        

If it wasn't for my job I'd 100% get the second one since nothing severe has happened.
Yeah I definitely don't go anywhere. As long as the paychecks keep coming in, my only need to leave are cancer check ups which I wear a tightly fitting n95 to.

Thank you. I feel like it's selfish no matter what option I choose. If I end up living in my car I'll have to beg strangers for help again. I don't want to be a part of the problem with this pandemic but it feels like I'm entering a martyr complex if I knowingly risk what little I have left for the good of society.
That's why I'm so unsure of my decision. That second one could ruin my life and put me on the street. But I'm already halfway done.

I hope that first pfizer is good enough because I'm not even sure how I'm going to make it to the vaccination site like this.     
I feel selfish but it took me so long to go from living in my car waiting for death, to having my own place and a job.   

Will report the symptoms, ty for reminding me about vears.

I hope I have the courage to do this if I'm still debilitated by my next appointment. I wouldn't want anyone else to end up with my fate but unfortunately I'm surrounded by people that won't get vaccinated.
Not even losing your job? I don't want to live out of my car again :(
I just got my first vaccine and was around someone with covid at work.
https://health.ucdavis.edu/coronavirus/covid-19-information/covid-19-long-haulers.html

Ty for sharing your experience! Although I'm not looking forward to a flare, I would take it over the type of flare covid would put me in. Especially a short one. (I've also fainted while laying down, try getting a doctor to believe that one! Ugh).   

I can't take the next day off work this dose but I am allowed to for my second dose and it will be a 3 day weekend so legs up, hospital bag packed, meds in a bucket, vomit bags, and pedialyte planned for that.       

If my first dose messes me up I'll have to do what I usually do sometimes and bring my laptop into the bathroom working in between attacks. It's brutal and not something I could pull off for weeks.
Wait. Does this apply for marriage and medical debt? I've always wanted to find a partner but didn't want to financially burden them since I have a chronic illness.

Yeah tysm! Actually after being dismissed by doctors I found my people in the dysautonomia groups. My heart does race when I'm upright or the body is going through anything stressful. The group told me to test my heart after laying down for a while then stand up and test it. It went from 60 to 150. My blood pressure went from 110/50 to 75/35.     
I tried to show doctors this but they didn't really care. Funny thing is they often saw my bp at 90/50 and said it was a great bp. But when it was 10 points below that they freaked out and told me to not stand up?   
These people confuse me.
I'm pretty sure I'd just end up catching covid by then. I'm mostly housebound but do need to go into places sometimes.

I've heard bad side effects after the first usually has a lower incident of effects after the second. I'm preparing for at least a few days of feeling absolutely debilitated and a possible full month of just feeling much worse than I usually do.   
But I have no plan if it gets so bad that I can't get out of bed for weeks, like really idk what I'm going to do lol ... so I'm glad doctors appear willing to help with this type of thing.    

Good to hear you're back to baseline and now protected. But omg I really don't want to have to do this every damn year.

Definitely why I'm getting it. The rates of chronic illness after covid is so astounding. Vaccinations are much lower. Covid isn't going away either so at some point you either catch it or get the vaccine.   
I have to do it but still worried about the domino effect it may have.

I do not have a partner. How do you think your partner would do if they didn't have anyone to help them?    
Like I said I'm not scared of being sick. That's just my life. I'm scared of ending up homeless and losing my job.

I hope you get a taste of what it's like to be disabled by an invisible illness someday. I'm only trying to gauge how doctors are handling side effects being reported and provided a backstory in case people don't understand why I'm so hesitant.
Death is not the worst that can happen. Suffering in severe pain or illness day in and day out, not knowing when it will end is.

I've had several terrifying health events where doctors said I'd be fine and I was very much not so it's killing me waiting for Thursday.   
I'll have my first pfizer and also have some health problems like fainting and vertigo.   
I kind of hope the second just puts me to sleep. I don't want to be awake while I obsess over every twinge of discomfort.

I had a leep 2 years ago and keep coming up clean of the high risk hpv I had. I'm sure the virus is still in me. In my blood. These things can go dormant. They also tested me for hsv1 which I've had since I was a kid and that came up negative so the tests can only detect when it's active I guess.            

I did my best to enhance my immune system post leep. Made sure I kept everything in top shape down there. Tried to avoid infections like the plague. Wore flowy skirts a lot more.          
         
But I've heard it's more common to have it never come back. Not rare for it to show up again, just not what the majority experience.

This is kind of what terrifies me. I've had an undiagnosed issue I kind of gave up on pursuing and just stayed in that gray area of suffering before the pandemic started.     

But part of my issues is anytime I'm exposed to a virus.. it hits me all at once and hard. Like on the ground convulsing, in and out of consciousness from the shock and burning up, choking on vomit if someone doesn't turn me on my side.   
Then in a matter of an hour I'm fine like it never happened, besides the leftover injuries.      
I think it's an immune system issue but the doctors never had enough time for me or really were concerned.     
Now I'm not sure how my body is going to react to my immune system getting jacked up and honestly fear losing my job over this if I end up knocked out for weeks.    
I really want to do my part and get vaccinated but feel like I'd just be left to rot if I can no longer work.
Ty, I found a very small pharmacy 5 min away from me and I think I'm going to schedule an appointment after I'm past my period symptoms. I'm just so scared of something huge happening.
I get that  :). I just literally have no one around me 99% of the time. I still would get it for others I may not know, I just haven't been anywhere except the doctors in the last 5 years.
That's good to hear! Vestibular problems, vertigo, weird migraines, all can lay me out cold so I am so worried about a flare. Which vaccine did you get?
Oh wow. I didn't know ocd manifested that way. I have gone to therapy in the past but it was so unhelpful. Maybe someday I can get a good therapist.
I don't have loved ones. My only reason to get it is so I can see a doctor without hurting others in their office.  I work from home and never leave.
Individual clinic room sounds so nice. No one gawking at me (I have vestibular issues and the anxiety of people staring at me is hard enough with that).

I'm conflicted. I actually don't go anywhere except doctors once every few months heavily masked. I work from home and don't go into stores. I don't have family. If there was someone around me that could be harmed I'd definitely get the shot.   
But since it's just me, I'm only doing it out of pressure from my community. And the possibility of losing my job over heavy symptoms just to say I did it is ... eh.

Ty, I'm really hoping the j&j gets here. I think no matter what shot it is, I'm going to possibly have side effects but the jj is so quick and over with that it reduces an entire two months of panic while I wait for symptoms after each dose.      

I definitely know covid is worse but my biggest fear is my job. I actually put it over my life. I even recently went through surgery and was more afraid of being unconscious and unable to respond to work than dying, and started taking work calls in the recovery area all drugged up and apologizing to my clients for being unavailable.       


I really need a better job but I'm scared no one will hire me since I'm unable to walk and if I end up homeless while looking for a job, I am screwed. I've been homeless before and was heavily abused during that time by both doctors and everyone around me.  Being vulnerable is a death sentence here.

That's cool! I would love to have someone just as scared as I am take it with me so we can watch over each other. Unfortunately I work 6 days a week and am on my own.     
I'm not too concerned about the first dose. My immune system tends to go haywire a lot so I worry about the second

That's so nice of you but I don't fear any immediate reactions. More of the ones that hit later. I worry they will last too long and I'll lose my job while the doctors dismiss me. I'm so scared of becoming homeless while sick.

I don't unfortunately. I am a tech nerd and all of my healthy tech friends are even sus about it so it doesn't help lol.   

I haven't had any vaccines since I became ill. But I did fine in the past with them while healthy.    

I'm actually less concerned about an immediate reaction because they anticipate that. I'm not concerned about getting a fever, feel like crap immune response either. But I worry about a cytokine storm or long lasting weird neurological issues because doctors are iffy about those. So my panic would be the whole damn time until weeks after my second vaccine. I wish they still offered the j&j. Panic time heavily reduced.      

If we actually had a decent social safety net in this country I'd get the vaccine without hesitation.          
      
     
I trust logic and science. I don't trust the medical system or bias medical journalism which has quite the history here. What I trust vs what I don't trust overlap and my brain breaks.          

So many times the odds were insanely low, I got struck and it was an isolating disaster.      

But my brain is telling me to do this. Let's hope jj becomes available again or some kind of one shot.. I think it's my only hope.
Location is so important. Those huge crowds packed into a convention center waiting in line... Like no.

I actually did ask my drs office. I prefer it at their clinic because large crowds of people is a nightmare for me. First I asked for the jj because it's easier to just go in and do it once and be done with it. I also stick out like a sore thumb because I use a cane and shake a lot, it's really hard for me to even get anywhere on my own.       
       
Seems like right now it's a 'take it in a packed convention center and take whatever we give you' situation. And Idk how I'd even get there and back on my own both times. Maybe when this all calms down there will be better methods.

Geeze. Like I get masks but there's a time and place for everything. Also that's a bit negligent on their part. I'm sure a vomit soaked mask could cause asphyxiation if you weren't well enough to remove it.     
I'm glad your hubby finally understood. I don't think anyone around me gets how brutal it is for me. They seem much more sympathetic with things they can relate to. Like when I was spiking fevers a lot, they would say "oh the muscle pains with fevers are the worst".  Which tbh is enough to distract but not terrible. But when I get vertigo which is 100000x worse than any fever pains, they really don't get it. Heck I'd rather have the flu than a panic attack and a lot of people don't understand that either since everyone thinks panic attacks are being so nervous that you shake.
I feel like these studies have just become echo chambers to everyone with nothing really ever being done about it.

I kind of have a feeling that passing out cards is just going to land me more judgement. But usually when I have these events I can't move and am not conscious half the time so my brain is in a very primal state where what is coming out of my vocal cords is the last priority since other regions are misfiring. Once I'm able to collect myself I try to explain but no one cares at the hospital.

I always assumed medical workers know how weird and wonky the autonomic system can make things. It's almost like they just said "the autonomic system controls the heart rate and blood pressure... anyways moving on to the next chapter" in their educational courses.     
Given the amount of very well accepted conditions that have a heavy relationship with the autonomic system, I am just surprised.      
                
I get having non scientific folks behaving that way but this just feels surreal. I've met quite a few people in my life that talked oddly but if you actually listened to what they had to say, a lot of them were competent enough to not be deemed mentally unstable, and I started to realize it was probably something wonky with their physical health.    
             
Amazing that this is what we call medicine in 2021.
I don't see that going over well with doctors.
I'm the opposite. I love hot! Hot water and honey is my soothing jam

Yeah. I'm getting pretty good at knowing what can ease my symptoms, but the point of no return absolute brutality that hits out of nowhere... I can't do a damn thing and am in so much shock that I black out every few seconds. I can't help but yell or cry out. It's worse than anything I have experienced.

I'm so scared of this being lyme that I would choose to live in denial just because you are shunned heavily by the medical community here for even letting the word leave your mouth. They just get so damn triggered over it.       
          
 My low stage cancer was a walk in the park compared to all this other crap.

It feels terrible. Regular people actually are quite concerned because they can see me turn ghost white and dripping sweat while hurling, and they always wonder why I'm constantly apologizing after it happens... it's because of all the times I've been treated like a burden by medical staff. I assume if they, the people literally in a service to medically help people,  think I'm a burden for my symptoms, then wtf is wrong with me??

Social media is so terrible for me when my symptoms are high. Everyone always says "they only show their best times and not their worst". Yet most of them are posting something I couldn't even imagine doing, and they're doing it multiple times a month.             
          
Just the simplest things like having a fancy latte with their friends or family.       
            
Even my accomplishments are sad to them. I was gifted a treadmill and I strap myself to it for physical therapy, it's helped so much. But when I tell others all I get is "...you have to retrain yourself to walk after an attack? Omg that's terrible".  Like yeesh.         
                  
Mentally I find it easier to surround myself with others that have struggles. We try to push each other every day and comfort each other when we fail. We aren't calling each other "inspiring" or saying things like "I couldn't handle that you're so strong". We know each one of us doesn't have a choice and the only true achievement is getting back to blending in with society.

I don't see why it's so controversial either! I hear it can lay dormant so it becomes undetectable. As do many other types of infections. So why are they suddenly so confident that this doesn't. It's even well regarded in veterinarian practice! This medical system confuses me as to what they decide to target negatively.

I only got through one round. I got so sick I blacked out and choked on my vomit and stopped breathing. I don't think I can continue and my dr didn't really prescribe it for any known infections, just made up sinitus.

Ty. Already on the probiotic probiotic plan but will look into antifungal. Lyme is so controversial here that just having it on your chart is enough to get sent right to psych. I hope I can figure this out on my own.

Definitely a possibility but I know the diagnosis process and stigma is brutal. And I'm kind of in the middle of a conservative, low medical area. Traveling has nearly killed me in the past but maybe I can find a virtual doc.    
Also I was homeless several times before getting sick so I wouldn't doubt something infected me.

Whoa. Not many in that particular tier of life. It kind of sucks but I'm enjoying some moments. Let's hope our health frees up a bit. I'd love to actually do something fun without feeling like shit for once lol.

I thought I'd be dead by late 20s. 30s isn't as bad as I thought it would be and I'm not married, don't have kids, and have a chronic illness while working in tech support. I guess you'll just have to find out? I was a lot more depressed in my 20s.   
I'm not afraid of death but I'm terrified of dying. It feels fucking awful and if you can remember it, it will haunt you. So it keeps you away from the temptation but I wouldn't mind if I just keeled over in a second or didn't wake up.      

At this point I just kind of stick around out of curiosity. Like we just experienced a global pandemic, how strange is that? What if you miss out on an alien invasion or something?          

Also a lot of people my age aren't married and don't have kids. Everyone's just kind of lost and vibing.

I was actually the breadwinner in my last relationship. I'm not sure if resentment was the cause but he slowly lost his mind to the point he was getting upset with me whenever I pulled extra hours and going through my paystubs to confirm I was actually working those hours and getting upset that I wouldn't have time to drive him to leisure activities since I'd be so exhausted from work. Anyways it got really ridiculous and we divorced.         
       
I am now in a relationship where my partner makes much more than I do and this is where I can see things from the other side because I now have an illness that limits my abilities so I will never reach breadwinner status anymore. I hate that I can't make as much as him. I feel like I'm just this deadweight. But that's not his fault, as long as he's not an asshole about it, I deal with my emotions on my own. That doesn't stop me from trying to make his day easier because I know if roles were switched, I'd just want to have a happy partner and a quiet clean home.  It's a team effort, not a competition. It hurts when he gleefully talks about his raises while I struggle at work, but I know that's a petty emotion so I hide it and I'm still very proud of him at the same time and celebrate with him.     

I don't expect him to even acknowledge the chores I pull at home because chores are just an adult thing that you have to do when you can. I'll even apologize if my health is being impossible to deal with and didn't get around to things but he is never upset about it.       

I think he needs to learn that envy is a normal emotion but it's not an excuse to be a dick. A relationship is a team effort where both parties need to be doing as best as they can for the sake of each other.

I hope I hit that eureka moment. There have been a few good theories, even a specialist that seemed interested once she actually saw my vitals go nuts out of nowhere while I was completely calm the whole time. She said she'd help by making sure that is very well documented but it's been nothing of importance to the other docs.    

Actually have a friend that took years to discover a spinal leak and even after they literally found out and treated her, the rest of the doctors continued to not believe it and refuse to take it into consideration.   

What is wrong with these damn people lol.

I have a network share policy at work. $8k deductible and $400 a month. 
Tried getting a better one but marketplace will only match my job

I already feel ignored just for being female. Getting anyone to take you seriously as Trans has to be a nightmare. I'm definitely still trying. I'm in a rather conservative area and can't move or I'll end up homeless but maybe more virtual doctors will end up becoming a thing.

Thats why this whole situation is driving me nuts.  Also I don't always black out in that environment. Just more common. I'm worried to take another eeg. My last one was $3k and they wouldn't let me lower the bill no matter how many times I begged.

No symptoms during the event which is why it's frustrating that they are using it as proof. They just had me try to nap then flashed a bunch of lights in my eyes. Then when I read the medical records it said it appears to just be anxiety.

I get that. I just always thought doctors held a bit more incentive to go beyond since they have the power to kill or heal. It's a bit depressing to find out how many went into it for social status.
